title: Exercise 2: Yellow House Sports Day
instructions: Complete the following conversation with the correct forms of the verbs in brackets. The first one has been done as an example. (12 marks)
example: Mr Chan: Good morning, Yellow House! Our Sports Day is next Friday at Wan Chai Sports Ground. If you e.g. want (want) to join the 4 x 100m relay team, please sign up with me by Wednesday.

rules.form: v(basic) without the third person singular -s when -s is needed
v-ing without the verb to be
Use do/does/did not instead of am/is/are/was/were not, or vice versa
For a main-verb negative, use am/is/are/was/were + not instead of do/does/did not
For a will/would question, omit the starting modal and retain subject + base verb
For a will/would question, replace the modal with subject-appropriate am/is/are/was/were and retain the base verb

In every if-clause, include at least one distractor beginning with will/would. Prefer will/would + base verb when it is definitely wrong in the full context; where it is defensible (willingness, refusal, politeness or another modal reading), use a definitely wrong will/would + v-ing or will/would + past form instead. Preserve negative cues

blanks.explanation: Use 'were'. Hoi Yan is not as fast as Marcus, so this Type 2 sentence imagines an unreal situation: if + were, then would + base verb.
Use 'do not try'. This Type 1 sentence is about a real possibility, so the if-clause uses the present simple negative: you do not + try.
Use 'train'. Mr Chan is stating a general fact about the body, so this Type 0 sentence uses the present simple in both clauses.
Use 'would happen'. Hoi Yan imagines dropping the baton ('if I dropped'), so this Type 2 question uses would + the base verb.
Use 'practise'. This is a real plan with the result 'you won't drop it', so the Type 1 if-clause uses the present simple.
Use 'get': 'That's true for every athlete' shows a general truth, so Type 0 uses the present simple. 'Muscles' is plural, so do not add -s.
Use 'will we still have' to ask about a real possibility on Sports Day (Type 1). Put 'will' before 'we' and use the base verb 'have'.
Use 'issues'. This Type 1 if-clause uses the present simple for a real possibility, and the singular subject 'the Observatory' takes an -s verb.
Use 'becomes': 'It happens every time' shows a general truth, so Type 0 fits here. 'The track' is singular, so add -s to 'become'.
Use 'did not have'. Green House really has many strong athletes, so Marcus imagines the opposite: Type 2 uses if + past simple.
Use 'would not worry'. 'If I were in Green House' is imaginary, so this Type 2 result uses would not + the base verb.
Use 'do'. This Type 1 if-clause uses the present simple for a real possibility, with 'I'll be proud' in the main clause.
